newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up, but off highs on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up, but off highs on electronics.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher but off earlier highs on Wednesday as electronics shares surged on an expected price rebound for Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) chips, brokers said.
The index ended up 146.32 points, or 1.74 percent, at 8,576.94, off an intraday high of 8,636.93.
Turnover was a hectic T$143 billion.

Brokers said the buying spree partly reflected expectations of a chip price rebound following an announcement by Samsung Electronics on April 8 that it expected the unit spot price for 16-megabit DRAM chips to rise in the second quarter.

Electronics surged 3.79 percent, with chipmaker United Microelectronics and Taiwan Semiconductor both up by the daily seven percent limit to T$66.5 and T$90.5, respectively. Other chipmakers also rose sharply.

Motherboard maker Asustek, which is the market's highest-priced share, finished limit up at T$846 ahead of its May 5 dividend issue of T$15 per share, the market's highest dividend for 1997, brokers said.
"Expected DRAM price hikes give hope that semiconductor shares would enjoy recovery after their weak performance in recent quarters," said Jardine Fleming fund manager George Hou.
Brokers also attributed the rise to sound March export orders and industrial output data announced by the government on Tuesday.

Taiwan's March export orders and industrial output rose 5.61 percent and 10.01 percent year-on-year, respectively. Both figures, announced on late Tuesday morning, were higher than expected, brokers said.
Analysts said the growth in export orders and industrial output was prompted by a sharp increase in foreign orders for, and domestic manufacturing of, electronic products.
Wall Street's overnight surge also helped boost sentiment, borkers said.
Brokers said they expected profit-taking pressure to emerge in the market on Thursday after three straight sessions of gains.
"Profit-taking pressure above 8,500 points should be pretty heavy," Hou said.
A 8,450-8,620 range was seen for Thursday.
